standard.title: Establishment of the first British colony
standard.description: the causes of the establishment of the first British colony in Australia in 1788
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3: Students explored community change and diversity of contributions. At Y4 students begin studying colonisation of Australia.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the causes of the establishment of the first British colony in Australia in 1788.

nodes.label: European exploration as a precondition
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how European exploration of sea routes and the Australian coastline created the conditions that made British colonisation possible.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the journey of at least one explorer who contributed to knowledge of routes to Australia and explain how it enabled later colonisation.
nodes.typical_width: Examine journeys of explorers who sailed routes to Australia (Vasco da Gama, Magellan) and Australian coastline (Hartog, Tasman, Cook, Jansz, de la Perouse) using navigation maps; reconstruct journeys; explain how exploration enabled possible settlement.
wider: Compare what different European explorers knew about Australia and discuss how accumulated knowledge enabled colonisation
Investigate how First Nations Australians encountered early European explorers and what accounts of these encounters exist
nodes.hinge_reason: Without understanding exploration as a precondition, the causes of colonisation appear disconnected from historical context — the causal chain requires this prior context.

response_modes.reason: The causal connection between exploration and colonisation is not obvious to Year 4 students — build the causal chain explicitly through map-based reconstruction.

success_criteria: Names at least one explorer who contributed to knowledge of Australia's coastline
Explains one way their exploration enabled the possibility of colonisation

nodes.label: Reasons for colonisation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify and explain the reasons for British colonisation of Australia including the need for a penal colony, the American War of Independence, strategic interests and resources.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain at least two reasons why Britain colonised Australia.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the reasons for colonisation: Britain needing a penal colony; impact of American War of Independence; creating a strategic base in the global south; resources; describe the roles of Cook, Banks and the 'secret instructions'.
wider: Evaluate which cause was most significant in the decision to colonise Australia and argue for a position with evidence
Investigate how the decision to colonise Australia was viewed differently in Britain and by other European powers

response_modes.reason: Multiple causes give richer historical explanation than a single cause — the penal colony cause is widely known but strategic and economic causes are equally significant.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Exploring multiple causes teaches students that historical events have complex causes — this is a key historical thinking skill that transfers across all subsequent history study.
success_criteria: Explains at least two reasons for British colonisation
At least one reason goes beyond 'needing a penal colony'
